description: This bar chart, from the paper “Morphosyntactic probing of multilingual BERT models,” illustrates the Shapley value for three different language models—mBERT (light blue), XLM-R (dark blue), and chLSTM (light green)—across seven distinct linguistic categories labeled on the horizontal axis: L₄⁺, L₃, L₂, L₁, T, R₁, R₂, R₃, and R₄⁺. The vertical axis, labeled “Shapley value,” is scaled linearly from 0 to 80, with major gridlines and tick marks at intervals of 20. Each category on the x-axis is represented by a group of three bars, one for each model, with the light blue bar corresponding to mBERT, the dark blue to XLM-R, and the light green to chLSTM. The bars are arranged in the order of the categories from left to right as listed. The chart shows that the Shapley values for all three models are generally low across most categories, with the notable exception of the “T” category, where the values are substantially higher: mBERT is approximately 60, XLM-R is approximately 55, and chLSTM reaches approximately 80. In contrast, the “R₄⁺” category shows the lowest values, with all three models having Shapley values below 5, and the “R₃” category shows near-zero values for all models. The bars are not sorted in descending order; they are presented in the fixed order of the linguistic categories as labeled on the x-axis. No bars are visually emphasized through shading, bolding, or outlining beyond the standard color coding used to distinguish the models.
